subject: Assurance attestation runbook and inspection windows
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@veridianhealth.com>, Bob Cho <bob.cho@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Assurance attestation runbook and inspection windows

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the productive procurement call earlier. Attached is a concise runbook that outlines how Redwood supports attestation requests and limited-scope inspections (SOC 2 reports, log extracts, and pen-test access patterns). High level asks and proposed cadence are below so we can align legal redlines quickly: 

- Scope: production services only (API endpoints + dedicated GPU pools where applicable). No customer data plane access beyond redacted/filtered logs unless explicitly scoped and signed-off.
- SOC 2: we can provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a short attestation summary.
- Pen test / inspection windows: propose a minimum 21-day advance notice for any interactive tests; can support 48-hour standby windows for log retrieval during agreed windows.
- Evidence cadence: monthly snapshots for configuration & access logs; ad-hoc extracts for scoped inspections under an NDA and copy-limited SFTP.
- Technical contact / staging: recommend a staging token and a read-only metrics portal for visibility; SRE contact and escalation listed in the runbook.

Action items I propose: Laura to own the evidence packaging, Priyom to propose redline language for MSA audit clause, and I will coordinate scheduling and the briefing session with your security team. Can you confirm Veridian's preferred inspection window (e.g., 30-day notice vs. the 21-day above) and whether you require on-site/interactive access or will accept remote evidence pulls?

Attachments: RI-Assurance-Runbook-v1.0.pdf (runbook, roles, sample data extracts)

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@veridianhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Assurance attestation runbook and inspection windows

Hannah — thanks for sending this over. Helpful summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement note: Veridian requires a minimum 30-day notice for any inspection that might involve interactive testing or privileged access to production systems.
- SOC 2: we will accept a third-party SOC 2 Type II report, but we ask for the bridge letter (if available) and the control matrix mapping to our control set.
- Pen test: for tests that could be disruptive, we need a single-point escalation + a rollback plan (standard). If Redwood can support the read-only metrics portal + log extracts under NDA, that will be our preference over live access.
- Encryption: please confirm whether requestable log extracts will include metadata that could contain PHI identifiers. If so, we need controls and a sample redaction approach.

We can do a short kickoff call next week (Mon/Tue) to lock the windows.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Dir, Information Security
Veridian Health
alice.chen@veridianhealth.com

Subject: Re: Assurance attestation runbook and inspection windows

Alice / team —

Quick legal take and proposed redline language to accelerate the MSA conversation. Summary first, then suggested clause (high level):

Summary of position: Redwood will: (1) provide its latest third-party SOC 2 Type II report and a control mapping under NDA; (2) accept up to two limited-scope inspections per 12-month period with 30 days' notice for interactive/privileged access, or 14 days' notice for evidence-only remote pulls; (3) make available filtered log extracts and configuration snapshots under an agreed evidence-sharing mechanism; (4) refuse access to backend systems that would require privileged write access or secret key exposure.

Proposed MSA language (suggested):
"Subject to Customer's execution of the Order Form and an appropriate confidentiality undertaking, Provider shall, upon reasonable advance notice, make available evidence reasonably necessary to verify Provider's compliance with the security and privacy obligations set forth in this Agreement. Such evidence may include third-party audit reports (e.g., SOC 2 Type II) and limited extracts of configuration and access logs. Provider will not permit write access to production systems or disclose secret keys. Inspections requiring interactive access shall be limited to two occurrences in any rolling 12-month period and shall require no less than thirty (30) calendar days' notice; remote evidence-only requests shall require no less than fourteen (14) calendar days' notice. Provider may require a mutually agreed-upon scope and a confidentiality undertaking prior to disclosure and may reasonably redact sensitive infrastructure identifiers."

I've attached a .docx with tracked redlines for the MSA + order form audit appendix (see attached). If that language broadly works, Laura and Hannah can build the operational checklist and we can bake the clause into the order form template for the Veridian deal.

Attachment: proposed-msa-audit-clause-redline.docx

Thanks,
Priyom Das
